newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Jordan, Egypt hold refugee talks.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Jordan, Egypt hold refugee talks.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation, Egypt and Jordan held talks on Sunday on Palestinian refugees despite Israel's decision to stay away from the meeting.
Israel's absence, officially attributed to "technical reasons", was apparently in retaliation for a Palestinian boycott of all other multilateral peace talks.
The Palestinian Authority announced on November 26 it would attend only talks dealing with refugees in protest against Israel's delay in implementing interim peace deals signed last year.
Chief Palestinian delegate Zuhdi Said told reporters: "The Israeli absence creates worry among the Arab brothers in the region."
He said the Palestinians, Egypt and Jordan were meeting "as Arab delegations to coordinate and develop the work of the committee on refugees".
Israel and the PLO had been scheduled to hold the refugee talks in the West Bank town of Bethlehem on Sunday and Monday.
The negotiations were to have been the first on the issue since the right-wing Likud party defeated the Labour government in May elections in Israel.

Israel and the PLO agreed under self-rule deals signed since 1993 to allow hundreds of thousands of Palestinians displaced from their homes in the West Bank and Gaza Strip when Israel invaded both areas in 1967 to return.
Said said that Israel, the PLO, Jordan and Egypt have agreed in previous negotiating sessions to carry out a survey of the refugees and start work on reptriating them.

Under the broad 1993 self-rule deal, Israel and the PLO also agreed to discuss the fate of up to three million Palestinians displaced from their homes during the 1948 Arab-Israeli war after which Israel was established.
